newsitem.title: USA: White House reviews EPA national cleaner car plan.
newsitem.headline: White House reviews EPA national cleaner car plan.

text.p: The White House has until mid-February to review a final plan submitted this week by the Environmental Protection Agency on its role in a voluntary program to introduce cleaner gasoline-fueled cars nationwide, the Office of Management and Budget said Thursday.
The long-awaited plan is designed to help curb air pollution by supporting a voluntary program for automakers to build cars with lower emissions in all states but California.
The program, still being debated by automakers and the northeastern states, was proposed by carmakers in an attempt to stave off more stringent pollution control requirements.
The American Automobile Manufacturers Association said EPA's plan would be meaningless until the companies and northeastern states reached an agreement.
"A rule doesn't make sense minus an agreement with all of the parties," said Jay Hyde, spokesman for the AAMA. "Nothing has been resolved there."
The automakers continue to press Massachusetts and New York to give up their mandates for zero emission vehicles -- electric cars -- if the nationwide plan is adopted.
